name: ThreatPoint Intent Detection
author: ThreatPoint UK

sections.description:
ThreatPoint Intent Detection connects your WordPress site to the ThreatPoint Intent Evaluation API to protect your forms, pages, and REST endpoints from automated bots, unauthorized AI agents, credential stuffers, and web scrapers.

The plugin evaluates incoming requests against six real-time intelligence engines:

  1. DOM & Runtime Evasion Analysis: Detects automation frameworks (Puppeteer, Playwright, Selenium), headless browser environments, patched prototype getters, and cross-context iframe leaks.
  2. Kinetic Interaction Evaluation: Analyzes physical human kinetics (natural cursor trajectory curvature, velocity variance, click dwell intervals, touch contact geometry, and keystroke flight rhythm) without ever capturing keystroke contents or user input data.
  3. TLS & Protocol Inspection: Detects bot TLS fingerprint stacks (TPHash / JA4 / JA3), validates RFC 8701 GREASE extensions, and identifies protocol discrepancies.
  4. Physical Device Recognition: Correlates cross-browser hardware identity invariants (display signature, WebGL shader execution canary, and Web Audio DSP entropy) to detect device token recycling and velocity bursts.
  5. ThreatPoint IP Intelligence: Evaluates IP risk tier, Non-Human Traffic (NHT) signatures, hosting/VPN/proxy detection, ASN classification, and forward-confirmed reverse DNS.
  6. AI Agent Provenance: Differentiates verified search/AI crawlers (ClaudeBot, GPTBot, PerplexityBot) from unauthorized autonomous agents, scrapers, and spoofed agents.

External services

This plugin connects to external ThreatPoint API services to provide real-time bot detection, agent classification, and security threat evaluation.

  • Service Name: ThreatPoint Intent Detection API
  • Service Provider: ThreatPoint Cyber Security (https://threatpoint.co.uk)
  • Service Endpoint: https://verifyb.threatpoint.co.uk/api/v1/intent/evaluate
  • When data is sent: Data is transmitted when a visitor submits a protected form (login, registration, password recovery, checkout), navigates to a protected route, accesses a protected REST API endpoint, or completes an interactive human verification challenge.
  • What data is sent:
    • Request metadata: Visitor IP address, HTTP headers (User-Agent, Accept-Language, Sec-CH-UA client hints), and requested URL path.
    • Browser hardware & environment signals: Canvas and WebGL shader rendering checksums, unmasked GPU vendor/renderer strings, screen display resolution, Web Audio DSP canary checksum, and automation detection flags.
    • Kinetic interaction metrics: Aggregated mouse movement trajectory samples, click dwell duration, touch contact geometry, scroll direction events, and keystroke flight intervals (no typed characters or form input values are ever captured).
    • Anonymized device session token.
  • Terms of Service: ThreatPoint Terms of Service
  • Privacy Policy: ThreatPoint Privacy Policy

Source Code & Build

The complete, readable, unminified JavaScript source code for the client telemetry collector is included directly in the plugin package at assets/js/tp-intent-collector.js. It contains full comments, standard identifiers, and no obfuscation.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the threatpoint-intent folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or upload the plugin .zip via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin in your WordPress admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to ThreatPoint Intent Detection in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Enter your ThreatPoint API key and configure your enforcement thresholds and protected routes.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require an API key?

Yes. The plugin connects to the ThreatPoint Intent Detection API to evaluate traffic. You can obtain an API key directly from the ThreatPoint API team at https://threatpoint.co.uk.

Is there a free usage tier?

The plugin includes 200 complimentary queries to test and evaluate traffic before requiring a licensed commercial key from ThreatPoint.

Does the plugin capture sensitive form data or keystrokes?

No. The client-side telemetry script measures only aggregate kinetic metrics (movement curvature, velocity, dwell intervals, and flight time between keystrokes). It never reads, logs, or transmits form text, passwords, or personal user data.
